page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. The configuration delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores operating at 3.1 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 64 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a generous 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Complementing the core compute resources is 300 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results highlight solid throughput across memory-centric and multi-threaded tasks, contrasted by modest single-threaded compute metrics. The instance achieved 6.38 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and steady multi-core results in stress-ng and PassMark CPU suites. Memory bandwidth reaches 382.09 GB/sec for cached 16 KB read blocks and over 51 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads. Conversely, single-core evaluations in Geekbench and stress-ng placed in the lower quartile, and CPU-based LLM inference showed low throughput on 7B models.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of high RAM capacity, dedicated local NVMe scratch space, and balanced multi-core performance makes this instance cost-effective for caching tiers and transactional databases. While less efficient for CPU-bound serial compute or AI text generation, it delivers reliable efficiency for memory-heavy services such as Redis, in-memory analytics, and intermediate ETL staging.
description: Amazon Web Services r5dn.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, featuring an 8-vCPU, 4-core Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Equipped with 64 GB of DDR4 memory, the instance maintains an 8 GB per vCPU allocation alongside a bundled 300 GB local NVMe SSD and 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate average multi-threaded compute and solid memory throughput, demonstrated by 6.38 million Redis SET operations per second and 51.32 GB/sec in large-block uncached memory reads. However, single-core processing and LLM inference performance measure on the lower end. With its substantial memory footprint and fast local ephemeral storage, r5dn.2xlarge is well tailored for in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, and high-throughput data processing workflows requiring rapid local I/O.
